description: Human-review-derived golden expectations for Splunk SOAR connector PR review behavior. Expected patterns are based on historical AI/human review feedback and the detailed human reviews supplied for Microsoft OneDrive, Tanium REST, GitHub, urlscan, and Cyberint Premium IOC.
notes: The evaluator skips cases whose artifacts_dir does not contain review_input.json. Keep the case here anyway so a saved run becomes active automatically once copied under runs/.
Historical human reviews are reference material, not authority. A current PR must still prove the issue from its own code, docs, CI, or metadata.
Terms should stay behavior-focused so the bot learns reusable review patterns instead of overfitting to one exact PR comment.

pattern_catalog.summary: OAuth client-credentials token exchanges must match vendor docs, including HTTP Basic auth when required instead of sending client_id/client_secret only in the body.
Auth docs, asset fields, and executable auth paths must agree; stale OAuth/client-credential fields should not remain when runtime code only supports another path.
Token and API requests need explicit timeouts so worker execution cannot hang on network failures.
External API TLS verification should not default to false, and any runtime verify option must be exposed in app JSON asset configuration.
Do not log full params, API responses, headers, tokens, tenant data, PII, or full debug response text.
When code calls add_data() with raw API responses, app JSON must declare the returned action_result.data.* paths users need.
Summary keys emitted by code or preserved from legacy apps must be declared in app JSON or SDK summary metadata.
SDK output models built around raw vendor API responses should tolerate optional/sparse fields and preserve high-value legacy output discovery paths.
SDK migrations must preserve legacy nested output datapaths unless the compatibility break is explicit and justified.
Adding dynamic attributes to SDK/Pydantic output models after construction does not necessarily serialize those fields into action_result.data.
Poll Now and scheduled polling state must remain separate so manual testing cannot advance or corrupt scheduled checkpoints.
Do not advance checkpoints after partial container/artifact ingestion failure because that silently drops future events.
Timestamp-only SDIs, single-ID boundary cursors, and daily-feed-only checkpoints can replay or drop same-timestamp events.
on_poll implementations should use Poll Now, start_time, end_time, container_count, and artifact_count or clearly document a safe bounded alternative.
Poll-created containers and artifacts need labels, stable CEF fields/contains mappings, checked save results, and a defensible source_data_identifier strategy.
List/feed/dashboard pagination should have a maximum page/result guard and should not silently return only the first page.
Search actions must not interpolate raw user input into vendor search syntax without strict validation or escaping.
SDK migrations should preserve legacy positive-integer and non-negative validation instead of silently coercing floats, zero, or negative values with int().
Imports placed inside one branch can make a later exception reference a local variable and raise UnboundLocalError.
Custom action views should render completed action-result data, not create fresh ActionResult objects or re-call APIs from unchecked GET parameters.
Unknown action identifiers should fail explicitly instead of returning APP_SUCCESS by default.
Malformed JSONL/feed rows should be surfaced as errors or counted clearly instead of silently dropped while the action succeeds.
test_connectivity should validate low-cost connectivity/auth paths and avoid consuming production enrichment quota for a fixed indicator unless justified.
Large migrations and new make request actions need actionable offline tests; live-only tests, no collected tests, or import-broken tests are not enough.

Full SDK migrations should not receive a merge recommendation without collected tests, generated manifest/package inspection, and coverage of auth, metadata, output serialization, validation, representative actions, and error handling.
Generated manifest/README metadata must match runtime set_summary/add_data/ActionOutput behavior, including output datapaths, summary_type, required flags, defaults, contains, and cef_types.
Generic make request actions need safe TLS defaults, product-scoped endpoints, auth-header precedence, secret-safe parse errors, non-2xx output semantics, and focused tests.
Connector validation should cover positive integers, ranges, UUIDs only with proven provenance, non-empty normalized lists, page sizes, path segment encoding, and no silent truncation.
Auth-sensitive PRs should test every supported auth mode, partial credentials, token refresh, 401 retry, OAuth state validation, refresh-token scope requirements, and docs accuracy.
PR bodies, release notes, README output tables, defaults, dependencies, and migration notes must match the code and generated manifest behavior.
The bot should be able to approve or stay quiet on historically good PRs instead of forcing low-confidence comments.

cases.human_review_summary: Historical auth review caught missing HTTP Basic auth for client_credentials token exchange, plus TLS default, unsafe response logging, output summary mismatch, and failing CI/no tests.
Historical review caught auth-path mistakes around test_connectivity, missing timeout on OAuth token request, and checkpoint advancement after artifact ingestion failure.
Historical polling review caught same-timestamp replay because only one last_email_id was saved, and Poll Now contaminated scheduled state.
Historical output review caught add_data(response) while app JSON declared no corresponding action_result.data.* paths.
Historical docs/schema review caught README/manual claiming new JSON outputs while app JSON was untouched.
Historical security review caught cleartext logging of auth headers, token payloads, rotated token bundles, and token-creation responses.
Historical docs review caught PR body claiming a default x-tanium-integration header value that code did not implement.

Human SDK migration review focused on Microsoft Graph optional/sparse response modeling, upload completion model strictness, file memory buffering, upload-session retry/nextExpectedRanges, target_user_id URL normalization, and test quality. The saved PR #36 artifact has offline tests, so the stale live-only-test expectation is intentionally not active here.
Human SDK migration review caught ActionFailure UnboundLocalError, numeric validation regressions, get question results nested row-cell output breakage, dropped summary fields, and missing tests.
